root_cause.text: KVM x86 MMU's mmu_set_spte() handled noslot/MMIO PFNs before checking and zapping an existing shadow-present SPTE, wrongly assuming only guest writes could trigger present-to-MMIO transitions and thus leaving stale present shadow mappings when host userspace changed a shadowed gPTE.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `is_noslot_pfn(pfn)` MMIO-SPTE creation block from before the `is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)` handling to after it, and the commit message explicitly says commit `a54aa15c6bda3` "failed to account for writes to guest memory that are outside the scope of KVM," causing KVM to "install the MMIO SPTE without first zapping the shadow-present SPTE," which triggered `WARNING: is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)` in `mark_mmio_spte()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove in-function no-slot PFN MMIO-SPTE handling from mmu_set_spte() so that this special case is handled outside this path.
intent_record.what: The change removes a conditional block from mmu_set_spte() that checked is_noslot_pfn(pfn), incremented vcpu->stat.pf_mmio_spte_created, called mark_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pte_access), and returned RET_PF_EMULATE.
intent_record.how: At runtime, mmu_set_spte() no longer handles no-slot PFNs by creating an MMIO SPTE and immediately forcing emulation from this location; instead, execution falls through to the remaining SPTE setup logic, meaning this special-case handling is no longer performed here and is presumably moved or avoided elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle noslot PFNs as MMIO faults by creating an MMIO SPTE, flushing TLBs if needed, and returning emulation instead of building a normal SPTE.
intent_record.what: A new early conditional block was added before the make_spte() call to detect when pfn is a noslot PFN via is_noslot_pfn(pfn); in that case it increments vcpu->stat.pf_mmio_spte_created, calls mark_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pte_access), optionally flushes remote TLBs with kvm_flush_remote_tlbs_gfn(vcpu->kvm, gfn, level) if flush is set, and returns RET_PF_EMULATE.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes noslot PFNs to be handled as MMIO mappings instead of falling through normal SPTE creation. It prevents make_spte() from creating a regular SPTE for a PFN that has no backing memory slot, records the event in stats, ensures stale TLB entries are flushed when needed, and forces the page fault path to emulate the access.

Handle noslot PFNs as MMIO faults by creating an MMIO SPTE, flushing TLBs if needed, and returning emulation instead of building a normal SPTE.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is incorrect in-function handling of noslot/MMIO PFNs in mmu_set_spte() before zapping an existing present SPTE. This change removes that special-case handling from mmu_set_spte(), directly addressing the faulty logic path that caused stale shadow mappings.

The change directly alters mmu_set_spte() handling of noslot/MMIO PFNs by creating an MMIO SPTE and returning emulation, which is part of the faulty present-to-MMIO transition logic described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This early noslot/MMIO check is the core bug: it handles MMIO PFNs before examining and zapping an existing shadow-present SPTE, allowing stale present mappings to survive when userspace changes a shadowed gPTE.
This creates an MMIO SPTE immediately in the buggy early-return path, bypassing the later logic that would first deal with an existing present shadow SPTE and any required invalidation/zapping.
This return exits mmu_set_spte() before the existing shadow-present SPTE check runs, directly causing stale present shadow mappings to remain intact.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional introduces the buggy early MMIO/noslot PFN handling path in mmu_set_spte(). By taking this path before checking and zapping any existing shadow-present SPTE, the function can skip invalidating a stale present mapping when userspace changes a shadowed gPTE.

This early return is what makes the bug effective: it exits mmu_set_spte() before the later logic that would inspect and zap an existing shadow-present SPTE, leaving stale present shadow mappings intact.

This statement installs an MMIO SPTE in the premature noslot/MMIO path, reinforcing the incorrect assumption that the transition can be handled immediately without first resolving any existing present shadow SPTE.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant control-flow in `mmu_set_spte()` clearly enough to determine whether MMIO/noslot PFNs are handled before any existing shadow-present SPTE logic. In this commit, `mmu_set_spte()` now does an early check: `if (unlikely(is_noslot_pfn(pfn))) { mark_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pte_access); return RET_PF_EMULATE; }` before the later block `if (is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)) { ... }`. This is exactly the handling described by the fix: MMIO SPTEs are handled directly and early, instead of flowing through `set_spte()`. The old path in `set_spte()` that previously handled MMIO via `set_mmio_spte()` was removed (`if (set_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pfn, pte_access)) return 0;` deleted, and helper `set_mmio_spte()` removed). Because the vulnerable construct was handling noslot/MMIO PFNs before checking/zapping an existing present SPTE in the wrong place, and this commit moves MMIO handling into `mmu_set_spte()` with the stated invariant that valid-SPTE-to-MMIO conversion should be impossible, the function as shown already contains the fix and does not contain the vulnerable construct.
